changelog.title: Search by meaning, an easier phone layout, warmed fluids
notes: Search by what you mean: type warm, warmed, heated or cold and you get EVERYTHING that warms the patient - rewarming, warmed saline and LR, blankets, the room, a heat pack, a warm drink - across every tab. Works for airway, breathing, pain, bleeding, pee, comfort, falls, fever and more, in Find and in the new search boxes
Search boxes at the top of Procedures, Care and Bedside, with matches from the other tabs listed right underneath

Phone: opening a tab folds the monitor into the slim vitals bar so the tab gets the screen - no more scrolling past the monitor. Tap a vital for its live trace. Back on Chart, the full monitor returns
Care and Bedside are on the bottom bar now

Warmed normal saline and warmed lactated Ringer's (fluid warmer, 104-107.6 F). Active rewarming now says what it is (forced-air blanket + warmed IV fluids). In hypothermia, warmed fluids count and room-temperature ones do not
Big screen: an Aa button on the monitor to make it bigger or smaller (remembered), and the NBP block no longer overlaps

changelog.title: Big screen: monitor-sized keys
notes: On a tablet or TV the monitor now has real-monitor-sized softkeys, a bigger header, bed tabs, waveform labels and alarm limits - easy to read and press from across the room

changelog.title: Big screen goes properly full screen
notes: The device showing the monitor now hides the status and navigation bars and stays landscape - the monitor uses the whole screen
In a browser, the first tap also switches to full screen

changelog.title: Big screen: the monitor on a tablet or TV
notes: NEW - Big screen (Menu - Monitor - Big screen): your phone stays the controls and the bedside monitor shows full screen on a tablet, another phone, a laptop or a TV on the same Wi-Fi. Start a session on the phone, type its session number on the other device. A TV plugged in by HDMI or screen-mirrored shows the monitor by itself. Silence and Start NBP on the big screen work too. (Needs the new app installed from the download link on both devices.)
The monitor scales properly on big screens - the whole thing grows together instead of tiny text on a huge TV

Medical accuracy pass, checked against current US guidelines: about 40 drug fixes (correct US doses no longer flagged as overdoses, e.g. Narcan 4 mg nasal, oral potassium, Keppra and magnesium loading doses; routes that do not exist in the US removed; wrong teaching notes corrected)
Tests that diagnose a condition now show it (DVT ultrasound, STEMI cath, stroke MRI, CHF echo and more) instead of coming back normal
Epinephrine IV push into a patient with a pulse is now caught (anaphylaxis is 0.5 mg IM); oxygen at 1-4 L/min in COPD is correct care, not an error
The BMP includes calcium, magnesium can be ordered, blood cultures grow the right kind of bug for the source, the ECG shows the rhythm they are in now, and lab names are US (BUN, T. bili)
Realistic American patients: names that go together and fit the decade they were born, interpreter languages that match (mostly Spanish), and jobs that fit their age
No more same patient over and over: every launch deals fresh cases, and recent conditions and names are not repeated
Training content: Fahrenheit temperatures, potassium in mEq/L, US spelling, and a few contradictions fixed
Compression coaching now holds you to 100-120 a minute

changelog.title: New icon, gray dropdowns and a working Monitor button
notes: A new app icon: a live heart monitor, one beat being drawn at 72. It is now a proper Android adaptive icon, so the phone no longer puts it on a white tile (the icon comes with the next app install from the download link; everything else updates as usual)
Every dropdown (mode, case, saved patients, music, phone display...) now opens a gray list that matches the app - no more white pop-up boxes
Sign in, the account card and the patient files are gray like the rest of the app

Monitor button fixed: switching the monitor off now stays off (the phone used to switch it straight back on), it shows Starting... while it boots, starts faster, and a tap while it is busy is no longer ignored
Monitor and Pause show the right state even with no patient
The intro's name now comes up as the heartbeat sweep finishes - no dark pause - and the intro is a few seconds shorter
Intro: the box round the C is now a true square and the underline sits right under the name

changelog.title: Never lose a case - and five new songs
notes: Your case saves itself every few seconds and the moment you leave the app. Close it by accident and next time, right after the intro, it asks: Continue your case? - showing the patient file (name, age, MRN, what brought them in)
New Cases page (Menu - Patient - Cases): every saved patient as a patient file, with Continue, Delete and Save this patient now
Sign in with Google is now easy to find (top of the Menu) and has a proper account page. Signed in, your current case is kept in your account too, so a new phone or a reinstall loses nothing

Five new soundtracks with a whole band - guitars, brass, choir, taiko, a real drum kit, synth basses, organ: Unknown Toxin (heavy mystery), Trauma Bay (fast drum and bass), Good News (funk), Lab Results (electronic), Rapid Response (epic orchestral). 12 in all
The intro always plays Vital Signs; after it, the soundtrack you picked plays, and it is remembered
The tour now shows Cases, your account and where to change the music

changelog.title: More realistic medicine
notes: Allergies cross-react like they really do: a penicillin allergy now covers amoxicillin and Augmentin, cephalosporins cover cefepime, sulfa means Bactrim (not furosemide), and a contrast allergy reacts to a CT angiogram too
Serotonin syndrome now needs two serotonergic drugs (or a real overdose of one) - linezolid alone no longer sets it off
Oral potassium 40 mEq is a normal dose, so it is no longer flagged as 4x too much (an IV bag of 40 still is)
Acetaminophen is counted over a rolling 24 hours, so yesterday's doses drop off
Kidney stones, pancreatitis, burns and other big pains now actually hurt - 8 to 10 out of 10 until you treat them
Cardiac arrest: VF only ends with a shock. In PEA/asystole the pulse comes back at the pulse check, not in the middle of compressions
US infection-control wording: N95 respirator, isolation gown and face shield

changelog.title: A new score, and feedback that sends itself
notes: New music: six cues re-scored like a medical drama - grand piano, strings, cellos, timpani, a ticking clock and the heartbeat. Diagnosis (mystery), Code Blue (tension), Recovery (emotional), Rounds (documentary), Night Shift (calm), Rainfall (ambient). Vital Signs is unchanged
Email the developer now sends from inside the app - write it, press Send, done. Add your email if you want a reply. (Copy instead is still there if you are offline)

changelog.title: Update notifications, training times, no overlaps
notes: New: update notifications - choose All updates, Major updates only, or None (asked after the tour; change it in Settings → Update notifications). It never notifies you about anything else
New: time estimates in Training - the whole course, each module, each lesson, each practice topic and quiz, and how much you have left
First launch now goes: legal notice → tour → notifications
Fixed: the full monitor on phones was squashed into a narrow screen so labels, numbers and keys ran into each other - it is now drawn like the real monitor and scaled to fit
Fixed: small overlaps on the big-numbers screen (patient name and clock, Temp limits) and the power button covering a bed tab
Fixed: "N weeks pregnant" in a patient history was never recognised

changelog.title: Simpler Training
notes: Training home: one Up next card with a Continue button, your progress, and your path as a single list - the long rules are folded into How passing works
Each module is three steps - Learn, Practice, Quiz - with a step bar and one Next step button that always does the right next thing
All modules button on every Training page; on phones the module strip at the top is gone (just a slim sign-in line)
Same rules as before - only the layout changed

changelog.title: Updates show up straight away (for real)
notes: Fixed: right after a new version came out, Check for updates could still say "up to date" for several minutes. It now asks GitHub for the newest version directly, so it finds it at once

changelog.title: Updates show up straight away
notes: Fixed: Check for updates could say "up to date" for a few minutes after a new version came out (GitHub was handing out an old copy of the update list) - it now always asks for a fresh one

changelog.title: Legal notice wording
notes: The legal notice now describes Clinical Sim as a simulation for interest and general learning - not a medical course, training program or qualification

changelog.title: Welcome tour and legal notice
notes: New: a tour for first-time users - where everything is, what it does, the modes, Training, and how to email the developer. Skip it and it shows you where to find it later (Help & learning → Tour)
New: a legal notice on first launch (not medical advice, not a medical device, privacy). Read it any time in Settings → Legal

changelog.title: No more install warning
notes: Fixed: V1.25 made Android warn that the app tries to bypass its security protections - the part that opened other apps is removed
Email the developer is now in Menu → Help & learning: write what happened, tap Copy message, and paste it into an email to ClinicalSimSupport@Gmail.com

changelog.title: Auto updates and feedback
notes: The app checks for updates every time it opens, and asks: Install update, or Not now

New: Send feedback / report a bug (Menu → Settings, or Options on PC) - writes an email to ClinicalSimSupport@Gmail.com for you, with the app version and device so bugs can be found. Clinical Sim is in beta: please report anything that breaks
Tap a tab you are already on and it closes (phone: back to the chart; PC: the panel folds away)

changelog.title: Updates that do not fail
notes: Fixed: Check for updates sometimes failed with HTTP 404 right after a new version came out - older versions now stay on the server for a while, so it always finds one
If it still cannot reach the update, it says why instead of blaming the internet

changelog.title: Easy to close the Menu
notes: The Menu and More panels have a Done button pinned at the top, always visible while you scroll
The phone Back button closes the Menu, More and Find first
Tapping the dark area above a panel still closes it too

changelog.title: Updates you can install
notes: Fixed: the Update available window opened behind the Menu, so there was no way to press Install
Fixed: Settings in the Menu could be swiped sideways - every row now fits the screen

changelog.title: Pause button, smoother music
notes: New: a pause button at the top right; it turns into an amber play button while paused
Tap the yellow PAUSED banner to carry on
Fixed: crackling music on phones - phones now use lighter instruments and a bigger audio buffer

changelog.title: Procedures one tap away
notes: Procedures is now on the bottom tab bar (Chart, Talk, Assess, Meds, Orders, Procedures, More)
The Emergency button is red everywhere

changelog.title: A clearer, clinical layout
notes: New phone layout: a short header (New patient, Find, Emergency, Menu) and a tab bar at the bottom - Chart, Talk, Assess, Meds, Orders, More. Everything else is in Menu, grouped: Patient, Monitor, Help & learning, Settings
New: Find anything (the magnifying glass, or Ctrl+K on a PC) - type a drug, test, procedure or setting ("foley", "cbc", "tylenol", "chest x-ray") and it takes you there and highlights it
A calmer clinical look: navy and teal, medical line icons (stethoscope, syringe, pill...) instead of emoji; Beginner no longer adds cartoon faces to what the patient says
Music keeps playing properly during a case: it no longer fades out for every yellow alarm - only dips a little for red ones, and Options → Music → Lower for red alarms turns even that off

notes: Options → Phone display → Simple vitals bar: one slim row (HR, SpO₂, NBP, RR, etCO₂, Temp) pinned to the top while you scroll
Tap HR, SpO₂, RR or etCO₂ to open its live trace under the bar - ECG, pleth, respiration or capnogram - to check the rhythm or spot a missing wave. Tap again to close
A number flashes red while its alarm is sounding

changelog.title: Music, and a longer intro
notes: New: background music - 7 original soundtracks, each a full 3-4 minute song (intro, verses, choruses, builds, key changes) that varies every time it comes round. Options → Music: pick the style, set the volume, mute
Styles: Cinematic (Vital Signs - the intro theme, extended), Funk, Electronic, Pop, Synthwave, Lo-fi, Ambient
The intro is longer (about 16 s) and its music carries straight on into the app; the beat is the heartbeat on screen
Music dips while a monitor alarm is sounding, and pauses when you leave the app
New: Options → Phone display - Simple vitals, Monitor (numbers) or Monitor (full, with waves)

changelog.title: A new logo in the intro
notes: The intro logo: the C of CLINICAL SIM sits in a box whose bottom edge is level with the underline, which runs under the rest of the name
New: Options → Intro → Play it now, to watch (and hear) the intro again any time

changelog.title: The intro has a soundtrack
notes: New: an original soundtrack for the intro - a low drone, a swelling chord that brightens when the name appears, and a soft heartbeat on every beat the trace writes. Options → Intro → With its soundtrack turns it off

changelog.title: Check for updates works
notes: Options → Updates → Check for updates now works: new versions download straight into the app, no more installing APK files

changelog.title: Google sign-in fixed on phones
notes: Fixed: signing in with Google on a phone ended with "Sign-in did not finish: Failed to fetch". Android pauses the app while Chrome is open, so the sign-in now comes back through the Return to Clinical Sim button instead

changelog.title: A real monitor start-up, and a better intro
notes: The monitor now powers on and off like the real one: a start-up self-test before the screen comes up, a fade to black when switched off, and the button ignores taps while it is starting or shutting down - so the screen can never be flickered bright and dark
Switching off now fades everything - numbers and waveforms too, not just the background

New intro: a steady normal sinus rhythm at 72 written across the screen in real time, the way a monitor draws it (P, QRS and T on every beat), with CLINICAL SIM and its underline lit by the same light
Tapping the screen or pressing a key still skips the intro; Options → Intro turns it off
The chart now uses the full width of wide screens

changelog.title: Sign in, a new look, and a lot more real
notes: New: Sign in with Google (Training → top of the sidebar) — your progress follows you between PC and phone and survives reinstalling
New animated intro and a new app icon. Options → Intro to turn the intro off
Patients now fit their illness: realistic age and sex for every condition (no more men with ectopic pregnancies), and a history that matches

How they arrived: walk-in, family, ambulance with a real EMS handoff (and what EMS already gave), police, nursing home, found down. Talk tab: question whoever brought them — the scene, last known well, drugs, mood, suicide talk

Real people at real rates: some swear, grab, refuse you as their nurse, vomit, wet the bed or throw the tray — often with a medical cause you can fix. Care → Behavior & safety to respond (de-escalate, security, hand off with SBAR)
Defibrillator: the real crash-cart sequence (prep, pads, energy, SYNC, charge, clear, shock); VF does not always convert first time; SYNC will not fire in VF; pacing really captures; a talking AED
Monitor now matches the MX800 manual: apnea and RR alarms, real arrest alarm names (*** Asystole, *** Vent Fib/Tach), SpO₂ No Pulse, yellow NBP alarms, Silence acknowledges, audible latching
New training modules: Defibrillator/AED/pacing, Code status, Medication safety, History taking and patients who lie (more coming)
Getting around now grows with the course: 7 stages, each with a timed hands-on test
Fixed: the monitor came back as a stretched strip after minimising; DNR deaths can be cared for (curtains, family, a hand to hold)

changelog.title: Oxygen you control, lines you can remove
notes: Oxygen is now real titration: pick the device and set the flow (nasal 1–6 L, mask, Venturi adapters, non-rebreather, high-flow 10–60 L at any FiO₂). Under-running a non-rebreather or high-flow is caught
Ventilator settings when intubated: rate, tidal volume, PEEP and FiO₂ all change the physiology. Big tidal volumes are flagged; weaning the FiO₂ to target is rewarded

New: Attached list under the patient bar — every line, tube and device, each removable. Extubation follows real criteria, with a spontaneous breathing trial; extubate too early and they stop breathing
IV drugs now need IV (or IO/central) access; pulling the only line stops the infusions
New Options setting: patient arrives with an IV (EMS placed it) and/or the monitor already on. Never in training cases
Fixed: the chart kept saying "respiratory rate of four, snoring airway" after intubation — the exam and nurse notes now describe the patient as they are now
Fixed: a ventilated overdose kept getting worse — the ventilator now counts as treating it
Fixed: the monitor power button jumped position when switched on/off
The top bar, vitals and patient name now stay pinned when you scroll (PC)
Monitor training: new lesson on latched alarms (why it can say SpO₂ Low at 100% — Philips factory default latching; press Silence to acknowledge)

changelog.title: Know it, or you don't pass
notes: Fixed: the right answer was usually the longest one (half of all questions, up to 98% in some topics). Every question bank was rewritten — now it is the longest only 14% of the time, so length tells you nothing

Anti-cheat: quiz questions are timed (90 s, exam 75 s), leaving the app mid-question (ChatGPT, camera, anything) forfeits it — three strikes voids the attempt; no copying question text; screenshots blocked on the phone during tests
Guess detection: answers faster than the question can be read count as guesses; three in a practice set voids the set
Cases: throwing random drugs or a pile of unrelated tests at a patient is now a critical error
Progress is saved after every answer, with a spare copy; reopening returns you to the exact page; a test left half-way picks up where it stopped. Reset now needs you to type RESET
New: your license — name, M.D., rank from Pre-clinical student to Attending, earned only by finishing everything cleanly. Clearly marked as a simulation, not a real license; an edited save voids it
New: tap any underlined word for a plain-English definition (1,334 terms)
New: Ask the teacher — type any question; answers come from the course (on the PC the local AI explains them in plain words). Off during tests and solo cases

New module: Substances — what they actually do. Vaping, smoking, cannabis, alcohol, opioids and fentanyl pills, stimulants, nitrous, inhalants and how addiction works, with the exact mechanisms. Open any time

changelog.title: Training fixes on the phone
notes: The tour now scrolls what it wants you to tap onto the screen (body, CBC and the rest were landing below the screen on phones), and its box never covers the target
One tap on the body counts as examining in the tour and cases
Exit moved to the top-left; a Next button sits top-right
Exiting and reopening Training brings you back to the page you were on

changelog.title: Strict training, every module
notes: Training is now strict — you have to know it to get out: 9 of 10 to master a topic (one slip max, and a hint counts as a slip), 90% on module quizzes, 90% on the final exam AND 80% in every subject, 19 of 20 drills
Every quiz and the final exam are drawn fresh each attempt from the practice banks, so they can't be memorized; the final exam gives no feedback until the end
Miss a quiz or exam question and its topic is un-mastered — you have to learn it again before the retake

Cases: a coached run (hints, Show me) teaches it but never passes; only a solo run counts — 3 readiness questions first (one miss sends you back to practice), then no checklist, no hints, real time targets, 90% with no critical error

11 new training modules, each with lessons, Khan-style practice topics, a quiz, rapid-response drills and hands-on cases: Reading the labs, Procedures and surgeries, Sepsis (SSC 2026), Stroke (AHA/ASA 2026, tenecteplase), Chest pain and ACS (2025 ACC/AHA), Bradycardia and heart blocks, Anaphylaxis, Breathing failure, DKA and HHS, Electrolytes, Overdoses and antidotes
Labs and procedures come first: you learn what a test or surgery actually is and how to read it before any case lets you order it
New ⓘ button next to every lab, scan, procedure and surgery: what it is, normal values, when to order it, how to read it, and the traps
New lab: acetaminophen level (also on the overdose panel). The coag panel now returns a PTT — heparin raises it, protamine reverses it, liver failure drags it out
New rhythm: complete heart block (3rd-degree) on the monitor
Overdose case now teaches rapid sequence intubation (etomidate or ketamine + rocuronium) instead of an awake tube

Fixes: CO2-retainer oxygen explanation corrected (V/Q mismatch and Haldane, not "hypoxic drive"); epinephrine anaphylaxis dose is 0.01 mg/kg IM up to 0.5 mg; dozens of guideline corrections across conditions

changelog.title: Real training, real medicine
notes: Every module now teaches topic by topic like Khan Academy: lessons, then 10-question practice sets with Hint and "I don't understand this" (opens an in-depth explanation, then a fresh question). 8 of 10 without help masters a topic; the module quiz opens only when every topic is mastered

New module: How the drugs work — what adenosine, amiodarone, epinephrine, atropine, diltiazem, PPIs, octreotide, blood products and reversal agents actually do, and why they are given the way they are
New module: Seizures and status epilepticus (AES 2016 + ESETT doses), with two hands-on cases
New: Rapid response drills — a strip and the patient, 10 seconds to choose what to give; 18/20 to pass
New: CPR rhythm trainer — hold 100–120 compressions a minute, steady, 30 in a row
New hands-on case: a tachycardia that turns into a cardiac arrest part-way through
Practice cases count far more than quizzes: any critical error, a death or under 80% fails the case and locks it until you re-master the exact topics behind the mistake
Competency check-off: a random case with no coach, no hints, timed against real targets
Disease book: all 202 conditions — what it is, who gets it, how it presents, tests, treatment, nursing, traps, how common — plus a log of your own patients
68 new conditions at their real-life frequency (influenza, COVID, C. diff, TIA, pericarditis, hip fracture, SBP, DKA cousins, overdoses, OB emergencies and more)
148 realism fixes from a line-by-line clinical audit (US guidelines and wording; e.g. iron deficiency treated with iron, hydrocortisone in adrenal crisis, no FFP in varices, vancomycin in meningitis)
Care team: call the pharmacist (doses, allergies, interactions, reversal), respiratory therapist (airway, ABG reading), charge nurse (what you are missing) or hospitalist (they ask what YOU think)
AED mode on the crash cart, with voice prompts — analyzes, advises a shock, then 2-minute CPR cycles
Tests that work like real ones: PCR finds the actual organism, urinary infections show a real UA, type & crossmatch, tenecteplase, oral vancomycin
Skip training is possible — with a blunt warning

changelog.title: Training: learn everything first, then the cases
notes: Modules 1-6 now open one at a time: each unlocks when you pass the one before it (its quiz at 80% or better)
The final exam opens once all six are passed
The hands-on practice cases (SVT, GI bleed, cardiac arrest) moved out of the lessons into their own section, which opens only after you pass the final exam
After every quiz or the exam: a button to the next step, or to retrain and retake if you are under 80%
Continue button on the Training Center page always takes you to where you are up to

changelog.title: Training Center
notes: A full course (🎓 Training in the top bar): 8 modules, 41 lessons, 42 test questions, 3 hands-on cases
Getting around: a spotlight tour of every part of the screen that waits for you to actually do each step (open the tab, type in the search box, tap the drug)
Reading the monitor: every number and its normal range, alarm colours, Silence vs Pause, INOPs and -?-, stale NBP, alarm limits, shock index
Reading rhythms: 13 rhythms drawn live (sinus, tachy, brady, SVT, AF, flutter, VT, torsades, VF, asystole, PEA, paced) with how to recognise each and what to do
Tachycardia, upper GI bleed and cardiac arrest, per the 2025 AHA ACLS and ACG guidelines - each followed by a live patient with a coach that ticks off every step as you actually do it, with Show me
Final exam scored by topic (80% to pass); Retraining re-teaches only the lessons behind what you missed and re-tests it until it is right
New order: Type and crossmatch (2 units)

changelog.title: Leads off, probes off: the equipment acts up like real life
notes: Most alarms on a real unit are the equipment, not the patient - now they are here too, using the exact IntelliVue messages from the manual
ECG: RA Lead Off, LA/LL/V/RL Lead Off, ECG Leads Off, ECG Noisy Signal - the HR shows -?-, the trace goes flat or noisy, and the light-blue INOP tone sounds
A single LA, LL or V lead off: -?- for 10 seconds, then the monitor falls back to another lead (the INOP stays until you fix it)
SpO2: Sensor Off, NoisySignal (movement or shivering), Low Perf (cold or shocked patient), Extd.Update (BP cuff on the same arm as the probe)
Turning, washing and toileting patients knocks things off; confused, restless or shivering patients pull and shake them; electrodes dry out after a day
While the ECG is off the monitor cannot alarm on the heart rate or rhythm - the SpO2 is your only warning. Leave the leads off and the monitor tech calls
Fixes in the Care tab (Equipment): stick the lead back on, change all the electrodes, put the probe back on, move it to the earlobe, move the BP cuff to the other arm, see which lead is off
Several INOPs at once take turns with an arrow, and the minimized strip shows them too

changelog.title: Alarm sounds measured from real IntelliVue monitors
notes: Every alarm sound was measured from recordings of real IntelliVue monitors (pitch, overtones, timing, how it rings) and rebuilt to match
Traditional yellow is lower (480 Hz) and Traditional red is 960 Hz with its bright overtone; both now ring out for about a second instead of cutting off
ISO red: 5 quick pulses on 481 Hz; ISO yellow: 3 pulses on 360 Hz; INOP: 2 pulses on 240 Hz
A faint room echo between pulses, at the level measured in the recordings

changelog.title: Volume in Options
notes: Options now has a Volume slider for everything that makes a sound
It is the same setting as the volume slider under the monitor, and it is remembered

changelog.title: IntelliVue MX800 screen, alarms and online updates
notes: The monitor now looks and works like an IntelliVue MX800, copied from the screens in the real manual (without the branding)
Phone: the MX800 "Big Numerics" screen; tap the screen name to switch to Standard Waves
Touch any number to open its alarm-limits window: 10-minute trend, limit bar, yellow High/Low boxes, Alarms On/Off, wide/narrow presets
Alarm Limits and Main Setup windows, grey SmartKeys with yellow Silence/Pause Alarms and blue Main Setup/Main Screen
Alarm lamp flashes red/yellow (solid blue for an INOP); the number in alarm flashes; the crossed limit lights up
Several alarms at once take turns every 2 seconds with an arrow; a gone alarm stays on screen until you Silence it
The other beds along the top light up when they alarm; NBP shows its mode, countdown and recent readings
Minimize button: fold the monitor into one strip of numbers (on the PC the monitor window shrinks to a strip on top)
Real IntelliVue alarm sounds: Traditional (factory default) or ISO, in Options or Main Setup
Traditional: red once a second, yellow every 2 seconds. ISO: red 5 pulses + 10 s pause, yellow 3 pulses + 20 s
Red is 2 volume steps louder; an alarm nobody silences gets louder after 20 seconds; NBP MEASURE FAILED gives an INOP tone
The heartbeat beep keeps going under alarms, like the real monitor; no more flat-line tone or siren
Check for updates, and this update log

changelog.title: Clinical Sim on your phone
notes: Vitals instead of the waveform monitor
Sound, beep and alarm switches, volume and Silence
Emergency crash cart opens right under the vitals
